raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: AI-based return inspection reduced reported disposal rate from 25% to 6%, making automated disposition decisions materially more viable.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: returned item received → visual/condition inspection → resale/refurbish/discard decision → inventory disposition

raw_opportunities.current_friction: manual inspection is inconsistent, slow and can discard resellable goods
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: photo-led return case intake + defect checklist + evidence record + rules-assisted resale/refurbish/discard recommendation

supporting_article_titles: AGEST、パッチ適用後のテストをAIで高速に実施する「AGEST ZERO TEST」の提供を開始
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: URL-driven before/after regression exploration can work without maintained specifications or authored test code, shrinking patch verification from manual hours toward automated cycles.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: patch planned → capture pre-change behavior → patch → replay/explore → diff changed screens/flows → release decision
raw_opportunities.target_customer: SMEs and internal IT teams maintaining web applications without strong automated regression suites
raw_opportunities.buyer: IT manager, QA lead or application owner
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: prove that a patch did not break existing web workflows when specifications/tests are weak
raw_opportunities.current_friction: manual regression checks are slow and institutional knowledge is often undocumented
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: browser baseline recorder + deterministic replay + DOM/screenshot/network diff + human review queue + release evidence report
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A zero-paid-API regression evidence desk that records critical browser flows before a patch and highlights only post-patch differences.
raw_opportunities.why_now: AGEST commercially launched URL-led regression automation on 2026-09-28 and published benchmark evidence, validating demand for specification-light regression workflows.
raw_opportunities.evidence_notes: AGEST primary source says URL/test account can initiate exploration, comparison and reporting; their product uses local AI. Lovable MVP must be narrower: user-recorded critical flows and deterministic Playwright-style diffs, not a claim of autonomous AI equivalence.

supporting_article_titles: Meta expands Muse AI agent for small businesses
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: A mainstream agent can now connect a small business's storefront, books, payments, marketing and work tools while retaining approval gates for consequential actions.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: business tools emit tasks/data → agent proposes cross-tool actions → owner approves → action executes → evidence/status retained
raw_opportunities.target_customer: small businesses adopting multi-tool AI agents
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: control what an AI agent may do across connected business systems and retain an auditable approval trail
raw_opportunities.current_friction: cross-tool agents create permission, approval and accountability complexity that small firms rarely document systematically
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: agent action policy register + approval matrix + sensitive-action queue + decision log + connector inventory
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: An agent-governance desk for small businesses that defines approval rules and logs consequential actions across connected SaaS tools.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Reuters reported on 2026-09-29 that Meta Muse for Small Business connects dozens of business tools but requires user approval for publishing, messaging and purchases, making approval governance an explicit workflow.
raw_opportunities.evidence_notes: Reuters verifies integrations and approval gates. MVP is a governance/ledger layer, not a competing autonomous agent and requires no paid API if approvals/actions are logged manually or via free webhooks.
